text_fidelity_a:
LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+ I ADORE the idea of this kit! It is seriously awesome! There's no clean up whatsoever, so my little ones can "paint" and learn to their heart's content, and I don't have to worry about them staining clothes or painting the walls. If it was designed a bit sturdier, it would be an amazing "busy bag" item(without supervision).

When these cards first came in the mail, I saw that there was a white sticker(of sorts) over the card. Getting this sticker wet makes the picture show up. I knew without supervision, that sticker could be torn up quickly or logged with water. I sat with my boys as they took turns "painting" the cards. They were gentle! Still, as the sticker dried, I saw more and more scratches showing up, which means the picture underneath is no longer hidden(though you can still pretty much see what it's going to be anyway...the white sticker doesn't hide it 100% even with no scratches) I was disappointed that it ended up being so fragile.

I recommend letting your little one have a large space, so that he/she doesn't have to stack the cards together as they dry. We were on the porch the first time my boys used them, and I lay them individually on the porch rail. I stacked them when we came in the house, though. I'm sure that is part of the scratching problem. Unfortunately, that leaves out the places that this kit would come in most handy, like car rides, doctor waiting rooms, and church(for especially young ones). It also makes the key ring that is included pretty worthless.

The little brush is two pieces. You simply unscrew the top, fill it with water, and then put it back together. It worked well, and we didn't have issue with leaking.

Overall, once again, I absolutely adore the idea of this kit, but I wish the cards weren't so fragile.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

I think what makes these work better than dog whistles or scolding or time outs is that they can be targeted at the instigator, not both dogs. So if one dog is quiet, he doesn't get shot; just the offender gets blasted. They figured it out really quickly. They do NOT like to be blasted! LOL! And I think they actually compete to see which one can stay the quietest.

Got these to blast the dogs when they won't stop barking. They don't blast a targeted enough stream unless you are standing closer to the dog, like maybe six feet away, but they seem to work for their intended purpose. The chiweenie Bingo's the really rotten one, and the first time I used one of these pistols, I shot him once, he turned around and defiantly barked at me; I shot him again, same thing; then I shot him in the face with it, and he ran off into another room and stopped barking. The first time I used it with Doobie, a Jack Chi, he responded right away. (These dogs hate getting wet...but a dog who loves water would react differently. Still might quit barking, though.) So I'm hopeful these are going to get the job done. Only time will tell, but so far they see the brightly colored gun in my hand and quit barking.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Super Soaker Zipfire 3-Pack(Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game This game is played a bit different than the regular Monopoly games. There are some similarities though. You get four tokens (and passports), so that seems to limit the number of people who can play. The object of the game is to collect passport stamps - the person to fill their passport first wins. The game starts off with all the major stamps placed on the board - a specific sized one for each property. There are some generic gray stamps that stay in the bank. Landing on a spot you have the option to buy that stamp or it can get auctioned off. When a player lands on a spot that you have the stamp for - the owner is paid a 'Visitor Fee' (basically like rent in the regular game). Another difference are the Here & Now cards and the Chance cards. I think these are what makes the game fun to play. The things the cards can let you do makes the game challenging - just when you think you're going to get ahead, another player can use one of their cards and put a damper on your play. Makes for some lively social interactions (if you get my drift). The dice is a bit different - one die has a icon in the place of the 1 pip (sort of reminds me of the speed die). That icon is the 'Sneaky Swap', it can also still be the 1 in some rolls.

Overall I have to say I've enjoyed trying out this new game (can't say the same for everybody here). I think we're still getting use to the way the game plays compared to regular Monopoly. The games tend to be a bit short - about an hour, but that might be because we still stop a bit and look at the rules to figure out what we're doing. Plus, given the different international locations on the board, we sometimes stop and an go look up where something is. (Helps to keep a globe handy). Fun game - and a bit educational.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game

text_fidelity_a:
Pressman Charades for Kids - The 'No Reading Required' Family Game, 5" Yes my grandkids love this; they are ages 5 and 10. The 5 year old can read some words, but not all, so we keep him to acting out the picture. Whoever guesses correctly "wins" that card and that is the point system. 4 cards wins the game. If someone does not guess correctly, the "actor" wins the card.

I would say that for the younger ones acting out a picture, it is helpful to have them "coached" as they act out because they don't always understand how to act out in a different way that can make a clue understandable. For instance, our 5 year old had to act out the picture "feeding a baby", but he didn't hold his hands exactly correctly and he didn't know how to add some other actions to help us understand that, i.e., rocking the baby, or shaking the "bottle", etc. A "coach" can help the younger ones with adding additional actions to their hints.

I think it helps all kids with standing up in front of others, self-esteem, considering how visual actions are important and ways to get across a message clearly so others understand. The 10 year old often said "this is easy" until he tried acting it out in a way for us to understand what his clue was.

I highly recommend. Young ones will need some help in acting out the pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Charades for Kids - The 'No Reading Required' Family Game, 5"

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab

(Also never played but wanted to) So when I got the box and it was barely larger than two boxes of playing cards i went... Well it did say "tiny" on it. I picked up the rules three times and read through them, trying to figure out the solo player game before going "this is not fun to play solo". However we finally sat down and tried out the Tiny Dino game three players. Playing is rather complex involving a small board, cards, and game pieces. It took way longer than the stated 45 minutes, (and TBF we didn't finish all six rounds. Kids quit wanting to play) but that might be because we kept having to figure out order of play, rules and what cards do what. I like the complexity, but it just wasn't a game either of my kids (huge D&D and strategy gamers) liked. They also like rules to be clear, even if complex. So three stars.
One star off because it is hard to read and see in such a small format. One star off because it is needlessly complex, or at least not laid out easily to understand how to play without investing quite a bit of time. Half a star off because one player rules are stupid.
Game free in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years

Brybelly Sure Stick Rubber Foam Poker Table Top Layout Card-playing is a huge family event for us. Not just poker, but all kinds of different games. We don't have room for a separate game table, we usually play at the kitchen table. When I saw this product online (and found out that the dimensions are very close to those of our kitchen table), I decided to give it a try. There is nothing negative that I can say about it. Here are the positives:
* rubberized back prevents it from sliding around on the table

* attractive green color
* fabric surface resists stains
* the ability to roll it up after use and store in a conveniently sized carrying bag (with a handle) is a real plus!
* there may have been just the slightest funky smell when I first opened the package (I have a super sensitive nose) but that smell has completely dissipated
* perfect size (for us anyway); I'm sure it could be cut to fit a smaller table, though that would mess up the white outline

I am very, very happy with this product! It fit the bill perfectly.

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.

Hot Wheels Marvel Avengers Assemble Avengers 5-Pack [Amazon Exclusive] As superhero cars go, there really only is the Batmobile. That said, Hot Wheels has given in a go to design what they think are representative of the Avengers. Any purist will recognize many Avengers missing, depending who they consider the official team, like Black Widow, Ant Man, and others. All of these guys are members without question.

The cars look sharp. Like any Hot Wheels car, each is well-made. Below, I assess each vehicle, but note, it is tongue-in-cheek. These are toys. Iron Man and Thor can fly, and Hulk can jump pretty far. Those guys might have little use for cars.

Iron Man -- Red with silver. It should be red with some sort of yellow/gold.

Hulk -- Really? Does the Hulk have the finesse to drive?

Hawkeye -- His car reminds me of one the Munsters used to drive.

Thor -- Like the Iron Man car, it misses his overall color scheme. Needs more red. Old school body style, maybe 1974-ish.

Captain America -- Appropriately, red, white and blue.

Anthony Trendl
TreeFortBooks.com

text_fidelity_a:
Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera After getting an X12 over Christmas, and having an absolute blast crashing into everything while learning to fly indoors, I decided it was time to see what it was like outside. Flying an X12 outside left something to be desired, so I began researching to figure out what might fit the bill. After reading MANY reviews and watching a ton of videos, I chose the X5c. It fit my budget, and I got the impression that it truly was a great quad to learn on.

Well, after only a few short months of owning it I can say with certainty that the X5 has certainly held up its end of the bargain, and then some. I say "X5", and not X5"c", because the camera that comes with this thing is pretty lame. The angle (or field of vision, if you prefer) is very narrow. And I don't know if this is simply an issue with Macs, but I had to reformat the SD-card all the time- simply deleting files didn't work. Otherwise, the camera would believe that there wasn't enough space on the card and wouldn't record. So, this made it very easy for me to make the decision to jettison the camera all together, and just let this bird fly free. And I didn't stop there... the feet were no longer necessary either, so away they went too. The prop guards? Never even bothered attaching them to begin with. Flying this thing was kinda fun before getting rid of that stuff, but it became much more fun without the extra baggage.

From the beginning, I chose to learn on "advanced mode", just because it was faster, more responsive, and more challenging. However, I was by no means "advanced" at flying these things. The first time I took it anyplace that wasn't my tiny front yard, I took it to a local park and flew it up kinda high. Well, then I experienced that common thing where you kinda get disoriented with where the quad is in relation to nearby trees, and somehow I flew it into some woods with it impacting the first few branches at around 50 feet. Somehow, by some miracle, the thing didn't get hung up in any of those branches- I'm attributing that to the fact that it was still winter time (not many leaves to help hold it there)... so, where does it ultimately land? Where else, than in a creek? Yup! Brand new lil quad... in the creek. I just took a big deep breath and hung my head when I realized this. Somehow the thing was still on when I fished it out (it never completely submerged- landed in shallow area). I immediately turned it off and removed the battery before shaking it out best I could. Then I brought it home, opened it up, and placed it on the floor about a foot away from a space heater to allow it to dry out for the rest of the day. The next morning, I put everything back together, popped the recharged battery back in, and everything worked perfectly. From then on, I became much more careful about flying at any sort of altitude that included potential trees... and creeks, for that matter. It also didn't take me long to see the need for more batteries. I bought one of the packages available here on Amazon, where it provides you with four batteries and a 4x1 charger to charge them all simultaneously. I also bought to extra batteries before getting the 4x1. So, now that I have 7 batteries, I find myself not only enjoying the thing more, personally, I also have found more time to teach others how to fly it.

O, and before I forget... another sad, yet awesome, thing that happened: I was on my way to go begin my marathon of marathon study sessions for finals when I stopped by at a nearby church to catch about 10 minutes of flight time. I parked in a different area than usual so that I could see what range I could accomplish, and then flew it back with more altitude and speed than I'd intended.... well, I didn't turn fast enough and right behind me was a nice tree waiting to catch the quad. It got stuck at probably 40 feet up. I found various things laying around to throw at it, and even when I hit it with a lightweight block of wood, the thing still didn't budge. I climbed as high as I could, but the branches became too thin and there was no one around to spot me if I fell. Not worth it. So, I just had to let it be. I thought to myself... o well, you need to study anyway. This thing was obviously only meant to be an ill-fated distraction. So I went on my way and decided that I'd re-evaluate the situation only after I'd gotten through at least half of the material I needed to cover. So, a week and several thunderstorms later, I returned to the scene to find the quad stil sitting up in the tree looking all happy. I devised a telescoping "pushstick" made out of an 8' cardboard tube and some quarter round. I tied a rope to it, climbed the tree as high as I could, and then managed to push the quad out of the tree after extending the "pushstick" to a length of almost 20 feet. Took the quad home, opened it up, and it was bone dry and with no signs of rust of weathering. I put it all back together, and it worked. No problems at all. It's amazing.

I've crashed this thing into everything except for myself or other people. I've let my dog chase it, and eventually she even got ahold of it. Still, the quad survives. It slammed into a road sign at full speed earlier today. It survives. I've put this thing through tons of punishment, and thus far, the only thing I've needed to replace is two of those tiny cogs/gears at the bottom of the motor (the ones that engage with the larger gears that actually spin the props). These smaller gears seem to have a tendency to slip over time, and then they fall off. I've gotten into the habit of performing a little flight check before each flight, and confirming that those are properly seated seems to have made a big difference. Still, I have extras now. In anticipation of eventually burning out a motor, I also went ahead and purchased an extra CW and CCW motor. The nice thing about the prospect of changing out the motors is that the new ones have a metal gear that seems like it won't slip like the little plastic ones do. I dunno; we'll see.

I know I'll eventually destroy this thing, but OMG it blows my mind how much it's been through and is still going strong. I'd post a picture of how beat up it is, but I'm afraid it wouldn't really do it justice. It's scratched all over, one of the props was bent and then reshapaned before getting chewed on by my friend's cat. Still, the quad survives...

Once I finally burn out a motor or somehow destroy this thing, I'll update my review to let you know how it goes. Overall, I'm getting a lot of good times out of it. Still learning new ways to enjoy it. Definitely the start of a new hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera
